architecture.approach: Port the existing platform-core crate from feature/m3-substrate file by file into crates/platform-core/, adapting the manifest and any drifted API. The crate is standalone, so members = crates/* picks it up without touching the root manifest. Dependencies are declared directly because the workspace has no workspace.dependencies; tests are excluded and belong to the test agent.

dataModel.flowDescription: The application builds a Registry, registers its Provider values, and supplies a TokenStore implementation. Reads and writes are always keyed by the tenant and provider pair; the crate itself stores nothing outside MemoryTokenStore, which exists for tests.

securityConsiderations.description: Every token operation is keyed by tenant and provider, so a well-behaved implementation cannot serve one tenant another tenant's token (CON-512).
The crate never reads the environment; MemoryTokenStore is documented as unsuitable for production secrets (CON-519).
The public surface contains no product vocabulary and no vendor workflow code (CON-106).

dependencies.name: tokio
dependencies.notes: Dev only, for the test agent's async tests.

risks.description: Stale port may drag in APIs that no longer match the workspace.
risks.mitigation: Port file by file; MSRV and clippy jobs prove compatibility.
Pin one major and cover redaction with AC-011.

risks.description: A trait crate invites scope creep into implementations.
risks.mitigation: Out-of-scope list and NFR-004 enforced at review.
